title: Measurement: Length, Weight & Capacity
description: Class 1 IMO — Measurement: comparing length (longer/shorter), weight (heavier/lighter) and capacity (holds more/less), with reasoning and everyday-maths practice.

topics.title: Longer and Shorter (Length)
topics.concept: Length tells us how long something is. We compare lengths with words like longer, shorter, taller and tallest. A pencil is shorter than a broom. An elephant is taller than a dog.

examples.problem: Which is longer — a pencil or a bus?
examples.solution: A bus is much longer than a pencil.

examples.problem: Who is taller — a baby or a grown-up?

recap: Length = how long. Compare with longer/shorter.
Height = how tall. Compare with taller/shorter.

quiz.explanation: A train is the longest of these.

topics.title: Heavier and Lighter (Weight)
topics.concept: Weight tells us how heavy something is. We use words like heavier and lighter. A stone is heavier than a feather. A school bag full of books is heavier than an empty one.

examples.problem: Which is heavier — a feather or a brick?
Which is lighter — a balloon or a water bottle?

recap: Weight = how heavy. Compare with heavier/lighter.
Big things are often heavier, but not always (a balloon is big but light).

quiz.q: Which is lighter than a watermelon?
quiz.explanation: A grape is much lighter than a watermelon.

topics.title: Holds More and Less (Capacity)
topics.concept: Capacity tells us how much a container can hold. We use words like holds more and holds less. A bucket holds more water than a cup. A spoon holds less than a glass.

examples.problem: Which holds more — a cup or a bucket?
Which holds less — a spoon or a jug?

recap: Capacity = how much a container holds.

quiz.q: Amma fills a tea cup and a big bucket. Which holds less?
quiz.explanation: A tea cup holds less than a bucket.

questions.q: Odd one out (these compare weight, one does not):  heavier, lighter, taller, heaviest?
questions.explanation: 'Taller' is about length/height; the others are about weight.

questions.q: Short is to tall as light is to ___ ?
Order from shortest: ant, dog, tree. Which is the tallest?

questions.explanation: A bag full of books is heavier.

questions.q: Riya pours water with a glass to fill a bottle. The bottle is bigger, so it holds ___ ?
questions.explanation: A bigger bottle holds more than a glass.

questions.q: Which is the lightest to carry to school?
questions.explanation: A pencil box is the lightest.

questions.q: A jug fills 4 glasses of water. Which holds more — the jug or 1 glass?
questions.explanation: The jug fills 4 glasses, so it holds more.

questions.q: A bucket fills with 5 mugs of water and a small pot fills with 2 mugs. How many more mugs does the bucket hold than the pot?
A mango weighs the same as 2 apples. If you have 3 mangoes, how many apples weigh the same?
questions.explanation: Each mango = 2 apples, so 3 mangoes = 3 × 2 = 6 apples.
